description: We are a team focused on developing real-time, intelligent health monitoring software for space exploration missions. We are passionate about the intersection of technology, artificial intelligence, and life preservation in extreme environments. Our goal is to build an autonomous, visual, and intuitive solution that assesses vital signs, detects fatigue or stress risks, and helps the crew make rapid medical decisions without relying on Earth.
summary:
VitalSpace AI is an integrated, real-time telemetry system designed for health and environmental monitoring. It is developed to track vital signs and hazardous conditions in extreme environments. Built on a microcontroller architecture, the system combines biometric sensors (for SpO2 and heart rate) with environmental and inertial sensors (for ionizing radiation, ambient temperature, and a 3-axis accelerometer that measures G-forces and detects impacts or falls).

To address the challenge of delayed emergency response in high-risk environments, VitalSpace AI employs an automated triage system with three status levels: Optimal, Warning, and Critical. By processing data from various sensors locally and in real time, the system immediately triggers audiovisual alerts—via an LCD screen, LED indicators, and an audible alarm—while simultaneously transmitting structured telemetry in JSON format for remote monitoring.

This solution is vital, as the early, autonomous detection of hypoxia, acute radiation exposure, or sudden physical incapacitation enables rapid intervention. This helps save lives and ensures safety during critical missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works VitalSpace AI is an autonomous, real-time biomedical and environmental telemetry system designed to protect crew members in extreme and spaceflight environments. Built around a microcontroller architecture, the system continuously monitors blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), heart rate, ionizing radiation levels (in mSv), ambient temperature, and 3-axis acceleration. By calculating the acceleration vector magnitude in real time, it converts inertial data into G-forces to detect high-impact events (>2.5g) or free-fall/microgravity anomalies (<0.2g). All readings are processed locally through an automated three-state triage algorithm (Optimal, Warning, and Critical) that triggers immediate audiovisual alerts while streaming structured JSON telemetry for remote mission control monitoring.

Hardware, Software & Coding Languages

  • Programming & Protocols: C++ (Arduino framework), I2C communication protocol, and structured JSON telemetry output.
  • Microcontroller & Sensors: ESP32 microcontroller (utilizing 12-bit ADC resolution), MPU6050 accelerometer/gyroscope, DHT22 digital temperature sensor, and analog radiation and pulse-oximetry sensors.
  • User Interface & Actuators: 16x2 I2C LCD display, color-coded status LEDs (green, yellow, red), and a passive piezo buzzer.

Benefits & Intended Impact By executing triage logic directly on the hardware (edge computing), VitalSpace AI guarantees zero-latency hazard detection even during communication blackouts with mission control. Early identification of hypoxia, acute radiation exposure, or sudden physical trauma enables rapid intervention, significantly reducing health risks during extravehicular activities (EVAs) and deep-space missions.

Creativity & Design Considerations Our team focused on human-centered ergonomics, fault tolerance, and scalability. To ensure astronauts can identify emergencies without looking at a screen, we combined distinct audio frequencies and non-blocking timers (millis()) with intuitive visual indicators. We also included hardware self-checks during startup and formatted the serial output in JSON so the device can seamlessly feed predictive AI models for long-term health trend analysis.
